segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Tech stocks reverse, Iran says more tankers hit mines, Colombia sieges, and a verdict on Huawei
bullets: Nvidia and Anthropic shares fall; Asian chip stocks sink
Iran's Guards claim two more mined tankers; Houthis hit Riyadh tower
Colombia: car bomb and a supermarket siege

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Wednesday, November twenty-fifth. Yesterday's tech rally gave back a lot of its gains. Asian chip stocks fell hard overnight.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard now claims two more tankers hit mines. A Houthi attack wounded eleven people in a Riyadh tower. A U.S. jury convicted Huawei. And Colombia had a car bomb and a supermarket siege.
Also today: a controlled blast in Iowa, a man leaving the country after a long fight, and a very full Thanksgiving week. Let's go.

segments.strap: TECH RALLY REVERSES; ASIAN CHIP STOCKS SINK
segments.headline: A day after the Nvidia surge, markets give some back

sources.name: AFP (tech firms back in the crosshairs)

lines.text: The relief rally after Jensen Huang's return did not last. A.P. reports Tuesday closes of S&P five hundred down half a percent at seven thousand two hundred one, and the Nasdaq down one and a half percent. The Dow rose nine tenths of a percent.

A.F.P. says Nvidia fell almost six percent after Monday's thirty-one percent jump. Anthropic's shares dropped below the eighty-three dollar price set for its offering. One page put the fall at thirteen percent, A.F.P. put it at six and a half. We will say: down, by a number that depends on who you read.

Asia took it harder. A.F.P. had Seoul's Kospi down six point two percent, Taipei down four point eight, Tokyo's Nikkei down two point eight and Shanghai down two. C.N.B.C. reports SoftBank down more than eleven percent. Those are reported quotes, not certified closes.

And bitcoin slipped under sixty thousand dollars. Coin Desk says November outflows from U.S. spot bitcoin funds hit a record, four point seven one billion dollars, citing CoinGlass. That is a claim from one outlet's data source.

segments.strap: IRAN CLAIMS MORE TANKERS HIT MINES; TRUMP: WAR FUNDED
segments.headline: Iran, the Gulf, and what each side says

stats.label: Iran's line
stats.value: No talks until seven conditions are met

lines.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy says three tankers hit naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, despite American air cover. A.P. reports no vessel names and no independent confirmation. Anadolu now carries a second Guard claim, of two more tankers, with the same gaps.

Al Jazeera reports oil traffic through the strait is down forty percent. Brent settled Tuesday at ninety-one dollars forty, per Dow Jones. Asian quotes Wednesday were lower, about ninety, per A.F.P. So the claims are not obviously pushing the price in a straight line.

Iran's side: no talks with the United States until seven conditions are met. U.S. officials met Qatar's prime minister. And Trump told the New York Post the war effort is funded through about the end of January. He said Democrats who threaten to halt it would turn a quote, total win, into a loss.
Two sides, two stories, one strait. Iran says it is mining and the Americans say they are protecting. No tanker has been named by anyone. We will keep saying so until one is.

segments.strap: HOUTHI ATTACK WOUNDS 11 IN RIYADH TOWER
segments.headline: Houthis, Riyadh and the road to Aden

stats.label: Threat
stats.value: Jeddah and Red Sea ports if Hodeidah hit

lines.text: Saudi Civil Defense says eleven people were injured when the Houthis hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district. The wounded were two Saudis, two Indians, three Nepalis and four Egyptians, per C.N.B.C. The Saudi-led coalition calls it a terrorist attack and opened an investigation.

The Houthi spokesman then threatened Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Riyadh strikes Hodeidah. No new port strike was reported. Separately, the coalition says air defenses destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura. It reports no injuries.
A Yemeni military official told the A.P. that Houthi forces advanced toward Aden, and government forces set up defensive positions. That is one official's account.

segments.strap: UKRAINE: LIBYA SHIP ATTACK, PUTIN VOWS RESPONSE
segments.headline: Benghazi, refineries and Russian sabotage warnings

stats.label: Benghazi
stats.value: Two Libyan naval officers died of wounds (AP)

lines.text: A.P. reports two Libyan naval officers died of wounds from the Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship at Benghazi, according to Libya's eastern-based forces. Kyiv says its attacks on ships off Libya were self-defense. Tripoli wants answers.

Vladimir Putin says Ukraine hit Russian oil plants despite a request from Trump, and that Russia's response is, quote, inevitable. He announced no specific operation. Ukrainian sources say drones set two refineries in Samara on fire.

The U.K. warns companies that supply Ukraine of a Russian sabotage threat. And in Ukraine, the Kyiv Independent counts nine dead and eighty-one injured over the past day. The rescued woman from the Dymer strike has died, making twelve dead there.

segments.strap: U.S. JURY CONVICTS HUAWEI
segments.headline: Huawei found guilty in Brooklyn federal court

stats.label: Charges
stats.value: Sanctions, bank and wire fraud, trade secrets

lines.text: A federal jury in Brooklyn found Huawei and three subsidiaries guilty. The Justice Department lists sanctions violations, bank and wire fraud, and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. The B.B.C. counts ten of twelve counts. The jury acquitted on racketeering conspiracy.
Huawei says it will keep fighting in court. Sentencing is planned for September twenty twenty-seven, so this story has a long tail.

segments.strap: CIA, FINCEN CYBER INCIDENTS REPORTED
segments.headline: Two U.S. government systems report breaches

lines.text: A.P., citing a person familiar, reports an unclassified C.I.A. system was breached and the issue resolved. Reuters, citing the New York Times, says some unclassified information on a C.I.A. and O.D.N.I. network was exposed. The scope is unclear.

Separately, the Treasury's financial crimes bureau, FinCEN, disclosed what it called a cybersecurity incident, with unauthorized access to part of its systems. And one outlet claims Microsoft declared its highest alert after a global outage. That last one is a single-source claim.

segments.strap: ABREGO GARCIA LEAVES U.S. FOR SPAIN
segments.headline: Deportation fight ends with a voluntary departure

lines.text: Kilmar Ábrego García left the United States for Spain on Tuesday. A.P. says it was voluntary, after officials and his attorneys said they reached an arrangement.
That ends one of the most watched deportation battles of the Trump era. The terms were described by the parties, not published.

segments.strap: DEMOCRATS WIN TENNESSEE SEAT; HOUSE MAJORITY GROWS
segments.headline: House, Alaska and the courts

lines.text: Democrat Victoria Broderick won Tennessee's fourth district, ousting Republican Scott DesJarlais. A.P. says Democrats now hold at least two hundred fifty-nine House seats, their biggest majority since nineteen ninety.

NBC reports Republican Senator Dan Sullivan conceded Alaska's Senate race to Democrat Mary Peltola. Alaska's lieutenant governor said the state ended its voter-data agreement with the Justice Department and told it to destroy the data it received.

In court: a Georgia judge ordered Fulton County to give the state election board copies of twenty twenty ballots. A federal appeals court gave Trump another chance to move his New York hush-money case to federal court. And North Carolina prosecutors dropped a felony charge against Democrat LaKesha Womack.

Trump awarded Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom. A House Democrat widened a probe of Donald Trump Junior's investment firm. And the president pardoned two turkeys. Those last ones were not controversial.

segments.strap: COLOMBIA: CAR BOMB AND SUPERMARKET SIEGE
segments.headline: Villavicencio bombing; Cartagena hostages freed, president says

stats.label: Cartagena
stats.value: Gunmen held about two dozen hostages

sources.name: Blu Radio via watch gaps check

lines.text: A car bomb near the government headquarters in Villavicencio, in Meta department, injured at least twenty-three people and damaged nearby buildings, per the B.B.C.

In Cartagena, armed men held about two dozen people hostage at a supermarket. Blu Radio reports the siege ended at one thirty a.m. President Abelardo de la Espriella said every hostage was rescued and one captor was killed.
That is the president's account. Blu notes no official health report on the hostages and no judicial status for the other captors had been released.

segments.strap: IOWA: ARMY TO DETONATE LEAD AZIDE TODAY
segments.headline: Controlled detonation set for nine a.m. local

stats.label: Material
stats.value: About 68 drums, 9,700 lb degraded lead azide

lines.text: The Army says it plans a controlled detonation of about sixty-eight drums, nine thousand seven hundred pounds, of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The time is nine a.m. local today. A court approved it.
The Army and reports describe weather conditions as favorable. As of the overnight captures, it had not happened. We will not tell you how it went until someone who was there does.

segments.strap: CHINA LAUNCHES SHENZHOU-24 WITH PAKISTANI ASTRONAUT
segments.headline: First foreign astronaut to board Tiangong

stats.label: Also
stats.value: Russian nuclear-satellite report still a claim

lines.text: China launched Shenzhou-twenty-four with astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi and Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. He is the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong station. The agency says he stays about a week.
On the other side of the sky story, the report that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite by year's end is still just that. Defense News cites German media on an assessment. Russia denies it.

segments.strap: SOLOMONS SIGN TREATY WITH AUSTRALIA; N. KOREA EXPELS SWISS DIPLOMAT
segments.headline: Pacific, Korea and China

lines.text: Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a treaty in Canberra. It names Australia the primary security partner and, per the A.P., excludes China. The Solomons had rejected a proposed foreign military base.

North Korean state media says it ordered the head of Switzerland's diplomatic office out within forty-eight hours, after Switzerland sanctioned a children's camp. Switzerland has not confirmed that. And China's anti-corruption bodies are investigating Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining.
Australia's October inflation hit four point nine percent. Trimmed-mean was three point eight, per the statistics bureau. Australian shares fell on the news.

segments.strap: GAZA STRIKE; MENINGITIS ALERT; ISRAEL CHEMICAL CLAIM
segments.headline: Gaza, Katz's warning and Israeli coalition talks

stats.label: Gaza strike
stats.value: Hamas security chief among 7 killed, medics say

lines.text: Israeli air strikes in Gaza killed a senior Hamas security official and six others, medics say. A.P. reports at least nine killed in the day's strikes despite the ceasefire. Gaza health officials issued a meningitis alert, with two hundred seventy-two cases in October against a usual thirty to fifty.
Israel's defense minister, Israel Katz, says Iran is developing chemical weapons. Tehran denies it. That is an Israeli official's claim, not a confirmed finding.
In Israeli politics, Gadi Eisenkot's party reached a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's party. His bloc still falls short of a majority, and his mandate runs to December sixth.

segments.strap: DELL, CROWDSTRIKE-ZSCALER, BOEING ORDER, SHEIN
segments.headline: Deals and earnings

lines.text: Dell reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of fifty-four point nine billion dollars, up one hundred three percent, with twenty-two billion in A.I. server revenue. It raised its full-year guidance.

Morningstar reports CrowdStrike agreed to buy rival Zscaler. And a China Southern subsidiary filed to buy fifty Boeing seven thirty-seven Max eights, seven point four billion dollars at list price, deliveries in twenty thirty-one to thirty-four. It still needs approvals.
Shein agreed to pay one hundred million dollars to settle F.T.C. claims, without admitting liability. Xiaomi's quarterly profit fell sixty-eight percent. It blamed expensive memory chips.

segments.strap: BANGLADESH RAISES GARMENT MINIMUM WAGE 36%
segments.headline: Wage board votes after weeks of protest

lines.text: Bangladesh's minimum wage board voted four to two to set the garment minimum at seventeen thousand taka a month, up thirty-six percent. The labor ministry must still approve it.
Workers had asked for thirty thousand. Their representative accepted the result with reservations. The factory owners' group says production is still suspended at four hundred eighty-one factories.

segments.strap: MEASLES: HOUSE DEMOCRATS PROBE CDC DIRECTOR
segments.headline: CDC and a Fort Hood ruling

stats.label: Mississippi crash
stats.value: Six dead after Gulf plane crash

lines.text: A.P. reports House Democrats are investigating C.D.C. Director Erica Schwartz amid the worst U.S. measles epidemic in decades. Schwartz said the C.D.C. changed how it reports measles-associated deaths while reviewing death certificates.

Three Fort Hood shooting survivors lost their final appeal to watch Nidal Hasan's execution. And a Cessna crashed in the Gulf of Mexico off Mississippi. The Coast Guard says all six aboard died, including two boys, eight and ten.

segments.strap: THANKSGIVING STORMS, BAY AREA KING TIDES
segments.headline: Storms, floods and holiday travel

stats.label: Thursday
stats.value: Heavy rain, wind, flooding: Ohio Valley to New England

stats.label: Indonesia
stats.value: Dozens trapped in flooded gold mine

lines.text: NOAA forecasts coastal storms, rain and mountain snow for Thanksgiving travel. Heavy rain, wind and flooding are expected from the Ohio Valley to southern New England on Thursday. Storms also threaten the Macy's parade, per NBC.
On the West Coast, record king tides flooded Bay Area roads, per the New York Times and the Chronicle. And in Indonesia, rescuers are searching for dozens trapped in a flooded gold mine.

segments.strap: SENEGAL GETS AFRICA CUP TITLE BACK; REAL MADRID ROUT PSV
segments.headline: Sports, Wednesday

lines.text: The Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstated Senegal as the twenty twenty-five Africa Cup of Nations champion, restoring the original one-nil result and overturning Morocco's later administrative win.

In the Champions League, Real Madrid beat PSV five to one. Manchester City drew two-two with Napoli. The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph starting against Denver. And Jannik Sinner had minor knee surgery. His Australian Open return is uncertain.

segments.strap: ALSO TODAY
segments.headline: Quick hits

lines.text: Two people were arrested over a suspected burglary at the Prince and Princess of Wales's Norfolk estate. The B.B.C. and NBC report Thomas Markle was indicted on child sexual abuse material charges.

Walmart says shoppers can use Meta's Muse A.I. agent to search and check out Black Friday deals, with spending limits. NASA paused science operations on Perseverance and Mars Odyssey for separate technical problems. Google fixed fifty-three Nest Hub flaws.
Apple's French series Carême won Drama Series at the International Emmys. And the U.K. will give nuclear test veterans a full independent panel, per the Guardian and B.B.C.

lines.text: That's Heartbeat News for Wednesday. A new show every day by morning. I'm AI Robot Vex.

And I'm Alien Joe. A rally reversed, tankers burn on one side's word, and a lot of people are traveling for Thanksgiving. Two sides in every account. We will tell you what happened, and who said it. Take care of each other.
